Bug_Title: ICAST: int value converted to long and used as absolute time (ICAST_INT_2_LONG_AS_INSTANT)
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the getMalformedDate method. It performs an integer multiplication and then converts the result to a long. This can lead to incorrect results for large integer values, causing them to overflow and result in incorrect absolute time values.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when the showBug method is called. This method uses a value that will overflow when multiplied by 1000 in the getMalformedDate method, causing an incorrect absolute time value to be created.
Test_Run_Result:
JUnit version 4.13.2
.Malformed date for seconds=2147483647: Wed Dec 31 23:59:59 UTC 1969

Time: 0.031

OK (1 test)
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results confirm the presence of the bug. The test run demonstrates that the getMalformedDate method, which is supposed to convert seconds since the epoch into a Date, fails for dates after 2037. This is because the multiplication is done using 32-bit arithmetic, and then converted to a 64-bit value. As a result, only dates in December 1969 and January 1970 can be represented, which is outside the expected range.
